prompt: Ransomware compromised the update-distribution infrastructure for our EU-sold IoT product line. Does the CRA require us to report this, and on what timeline?
assertions: Identifies this as a potential 'severe incident' under Art. 14(5): impact on the product's ability to protect availability/authenticity/integrity/confidentiality of sensitive data or functions, or introduction/execution of malicious code — update infrastructure compromise plainly qualifies

Gives the severe-incident clock: 24-hour early warning, 72-hour notification, and final report within ONE MONTH after the 72-hour notification (distinct from the 14-day post-fix rule for exploited vulnerabilities)
States reporting goes through the ENISA Single Reporting Platform to the main-establishment CSIRT and ENISA, in force since September 11, 2026
Distinguishes CRA reporting from other regimes where relevant (e.g., GDPR breach notification or NIS2 may apply in parallel to different actors/facts)
Notes awareness-based timing and advises documenting the awareness moment and assessment
